rho_reference.protocol: research/mt_timed_20261112/PROTOCOL.md: per configuration, the fastest (solve-phase wall time, median of 3 interleaved repeats) of 10 runs of this harness's multi-target rho (Kuhn-Struik retention rho rho2xks x 4 kappa, distinguished-point rho rhodpu x 6), x-only / negation-map classes
rho_reference.unit: solve-phase wall time on one pinned CPU of the session VM (diagnostic); the gae_band below is the counted GAE per target (I = 10M, S = M, h on hash-table, solver and native operations) of the time-fastest keys
rho_reference.binary_or_process: target/release/examples/mt_fieldops built from commit a992ed6c80 (bin_sha256 in every row of runs.jsonl), same binary for every arm
rho_reference.note: Wall-time study; band shown for the counted cost of the time-fastest IC and rho keys at 32 b, T = 16384 (medians over 4 configurations). strongest_available = the strongest multi-target rho in this harness (validated in research/mt_fieldops_v5_20261112); not ecbench's rho.multitarget_pooled. Seconds are diagnostic (session VM, not an isolated L2 node). The counted band of these time-fastest keys favours the IC at every h, while their wall time favours rho at 2^32: the counted model with one h for hash and native work does not predict this host's timing (native work is nearly free, lookups are not).
